ERIOR REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT Francisco Gold Condominium II, EDSAcor. Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City OF UNDERSEQETARY FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT 12 June 2008 NG. 43 S. MS. EMMA LOURDES C. DE Barangay Kagawads Barangay Siena, Quezon City Gentlemen/Ladies: This pertains to your letter inquiring from this Department the following matters raised, to wit: 1. "Salaries of personal staff of Punong Barangay Benjamin Rivera. Those people were appointed only by the Punong Barangay without discussing (sic) and approval of the Sangguniang Barangay since December of 2007 up to the present. Note that the Barangay elected officials has (sic) not yet received any remuneration since December of 2007 despite our verbal and written demands. In order for us, barangay elected official to receive our allowances, the punong barangay is insisting to state the names of his personnel into the payroll and receive salaries even without proper attached appointments. 2. The Sangguniang Barangay Council had filed a resolution last January 19, 2008 concerning 3 check signatories as a requisite before check releasing, Punong Barangay, Barangay Treasurer and I Sangguniang Barangay member to protect the Barangay funds. Note that there were already records Of malversation Of funds and was amicably settled. Therefore, in order to eradicate the occurrence, the one member filed a resolution signed by the majority of the members for adoption but unfortunately the Punong Barangay failed to sign it."

-2- In your first query, you mentioned the term "personal staff' of the Punong Barangay. To our mind, such personal staff connotes two (2) kinds, namely: (I) those staff of the punong barangay whom he hired to attend to his needs and whose salaries are personally borne by the Punong Barangay, so therefore, their appointments no longer require the approval of the majority of the sangguniang barangay members; or (2) those staff of the punong barangay whose positions were created through a barangay ordinance pursuant to the second paragraph of Section 387 of the Local Government Code, referring to the power of the barangay to create additional positions as it may deem necessary for the operations of the barangay and,in relation to Section 396 of the same Code, are appointed by the Punong Barangay. However, when you came to this Office for a series of follow-ups, you represented and clarified that the personal staff that you were referring to pertains to the second kind. Coming now to your first query, may we invite your attention to Section 387 of the Local Government Code. Said Section enumerated the main barangay officials in the barangay government, namely: the Punong Barangay; the Sangguniang Barangay Members; the Barangay Treasurer; the Barangay Secretary; the SK officials; the Barangay Tanods and the Lupong Tagapamayapa. In relation thereto, and as discussed above, the second paragraph of Section 387 conferred unto the barangay government the power to create additional barangay positions as it may deem necessary for the efficient and effective operation of the barangay. The creation of additional barangay positions shall be done through an appropriate barangay ordinance, subject to availability of funds and the 55% personal services limitation on barangay budget. Along this line, may we emphasize that with respect to Barangay Secretary, Barangay Treasurer and Lupong Tagapamayapa, the Local Government Code provided for the specific manner and procedure by which these barangay officials are to be appointed. With respect to the Barangay Secretary and the Barangay Treasurer, Sections 394 and 395 of the Local Government Code provides that they shall be appointed by the Punong Barangay with the concurrence of the Sangguniang Barangay. On the other hand, with respect to the Members of the Lupong Tagapamayapa, Section 399 of the Local Government Code provides that the Members of the Lupon shall be appointed by the Punong Barangay from among the persons whom he deterrnines to be suitable therefor. In relation thereto, it bears to stress that the Local Government Code did not specify the manner of

-3- appointing the Barangay Tanod, except that under Section 396 of the Local Government Code, subtitle "Other Appointive Barangay Officials". it is provided that the qualifications, duties and functions of all other barangay officials appointed by the Punong Barangay shall be governed by the provisions of this Code or other laws or barangay ordinance. At this point, it is relevant to note one of the powers Of the Punong Barangay, particularly Section 389 (b) (5) of the same Code, which provides that upon approval by a majority of all the Sangguniang Barangay Members. the Punong Barangay shall appoint other appointive barangay officials. In relation to the appointing authority of the Punong Barangay vis-ä-vis the authority of the barangay, through an ordinance, to create additional appointive positions other than those mandated by the Local Government Code, may we note that the barangay ordinance so creating an office/position may provide for the qualifications and the manner of appointment to the occupant of the newly created barangay position. The barangay ordinance, subject to the wisdom of the Sangguniang Barangay, may or may not require the approval of the Sangguniang Barangay of the appointment to be issued by the Punong Barangay. Prescinding from the immediately preceding paragraph, we can, therefore, conclude that there are two (2) types of appointive barangay officials other than the Barangay Secretary, Barangay Treasurer and the Lupong Tagapamayapa, which are: (1) the Barangay Tanod, whose appointment would require approval from the Sangguniang Barangay per Section 389 (b) (5) of the Local Government Code; and (2) those barangay appointive officials occupying positions created by the barangay government. In the latter case, the barangay ordinance creating the office may or may not require the approval of the Sangguniang Barangay on the appointment issued by the Punong Barangay, depending on the provisions of the barangay ordinance which created the new positions. Applying the foregoing principles, if the personal staff of the Punong Barangay are occupying the positions created through a barangay ordinance and said barangay ordinance expressly stated that the approval from the Sangguniang Barangay is not required for the appointment issued by the Punong Barangay, then the appointment issued by the Punong Barangay is sufficient to commence official relation as employees of the barangay for those persons so appointed. On the other hand, if such approval is required, then the appointment of the Punong Barangay is incomplete without the approval of the Sangguniang Barangay and, thus, cannot create official relationship between the appointees and the barangay Sans approval from the Sangguniang Barangay, the appointees government. cannot yet assume the functions of their offices. If, however. the ordinance

-4- creating the new positions is silent as to the requirement of approval by the Sangguniang Barangay, then Section 389, the general law on the matter, will apply, in which case, the personal staff of the Punong Barangay shall be appointed, subject to the approval by the Sangguniang Barangay. It becomes imperative, therefore, for you to examine the nature of the positions of the personal staff of the Punong Barangay as to what category they belong. Corollarily, the act of the Punong Barangay in withholding your salaries/honorarium as sangguniang barangay members and made its grant dependent on your approval to include the names of his appointed personal staff into the payroll is in violation of Section 512 of the Local Government Code, to wit: "SEC. 512. Withholding of benefits accorded to barangay officials.- Willful and malicious withholding Of any of the benefits accorded to barangay officials under Section 393 thereof shall be punished with suspension or dismissal from office of the official or employee responsible therefor." In reply to your second query, may we invite your attention to Section 345 of the Local Government Code, which provides and we quote: "SEC. 345. Officials Authorized to Draw Checks in Settlement of Obligations.- Checks settlement gf obligations shall drawn the local treasurer and countersigned local administrator. In case Of temporary absence or incapacity of the foregoing officials, these duties shall devolve upon their immediate assistants." (emphasis supplied) Based on the foregoing, the local treasurer (the barangay treasurer in the case of barangays) is the one authorized as the signatory of the check for payment of obligations of the barangay. Also, the local administrator is the one authorized to countersign the checks. There being no local administrator in a barangay, and considering that the drawing and signing of checks is still part of disbursement of barangay funds, we are of the opinion that the Punong Barangay can directly perform the functions of the local administrator based on his statutory function under Section 389 of the Code, and we quote:

-5- "SEC. 389. Chief Executive; Powers, Duties and Functions.- (a) The punong barangay, as the chief executive of the barangay government, shall exercise such powers and perform such duties and functions, as provided by this Code and other lazvs. (b) For efficient, effective and economical governance, the purpose of which is the general welfare of the barangay and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code, the punong barangay shall: (8) Approve vouchers to the disbursement gf barangay funds." (emphasis supp lied) In view of the foregoing, we are of the view that the resolution that you passed authorizing three (3) persons in the barangay, namely: the punong barangay, the barangay treasurer and one (1) member of the sangguniang barangay, as signatories of barangay checks is legally infirmed. The additional signatory, that is, a member of the sangguniang barangay, is in the nature of adding requisites on top of those required under the law, such as the Local Government Code. In the case of Villacorta vs. Bernardo (143 SCRA 480), the Supreme Court held that additional conditions upon subdivision owners are null and void. Ordinances amending and so violating national laws in the guise of implementing them are ultra vires. We hope we have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, AUSTERE A. PANADE Undersecreta Legal:2 cc: The Regional Director DILG — National Capital Region LMP Building, Ermin Garcia St. Cubao, Quezon City
